name: Strength Foundations
tagline: Build the base everything else stands on
description: A barbell-first program built around the five lifts that move the needle fastest: squat, deadlift, bench, overhead press, and row. You'll spend the first two weeks learning bar path and bracing before any weight gets heavy.
details: Sessions run on a 3-day split (Mon/Wed/Fri) so your joints get 48 hours to recover between heavy days. Every block ends with a deload week — this is not optional, it's where the strength actually consolidates.

name: Hypertrophy Block
tagline: Train for size with a plan that tracks volume, not vibes
description: A push/pull/legs split designed around progressive overload. Each muscle group gets hit twice a week with a rep range built for growth (8-15 reps), and we log every working set so you can see the trend, not just feel it.
details: Expect supersets and drop sets in the back half of the block once your base strength is established. Nutrition matters more here than in any other program — under-eating will cap your results regardless of how hard you train.

name: HIIT Conditioning
tagline: Short, brutal, and over before you can talk yourself out of it
description: Interval work built on a 40-seconds-on, 20-seconds-off structure across kettlebells, sleds, rowers, and bodyweight circuits. Heart rate goes up fast and stays there — this is the session people dread and then crave.
details: Scaled for every level: beginners get longer rest windows and lighter loads on the same structure, so nobody is left behind and nobody is bored. Wear shoes you don't mind getting wet.

name: Mobility & Recovery
tagline: The session that lets you keep doing the other sessions
description: Slow, controlled work through end-range stretching, banded distraction, and breathing drills. This is the class people skip when they're busy and regret skipping six weeks later when something starts hurting.
details: Best scheduled the day after your heaviest lift session. No weights heavier than a yoga block — the goal is range of motion and nervous system downshift, not another workout.

name: Functional Athlete
tagline: Train movement patterns, not just muscles
description: A mix of olympic lift derivatives, plyometrics, and carries designed for people who play a sport or just want to move better in daily life — picking up kids, moving furniture, climbing stairs without thinking about it.
details: Technical lifts are taught with PVC pipe before any weight is added. This program has the steepest learning curve of the five — budget two to three weeks before the movements feel natural.

name: Beginner Bootcamp
tagline: Your first 14 days inside the gym, structured for you
description: If you've never trained before, this is the on-ramp. You'll learn how to rack a bar, how to brace, how to warm up properly, and how to read your own fatigue — all the unglamorous skills that prevent the early injuries that make people quit.
details: Runs for exactly two weeks before you graduate into Strength Foundations or Hypertrophy Block. No exceptions — by day 14 you'll have the basics, even if it doesn't feel that way yet.
